key_insight: Strong guideline recall did not translate into patient-specific evidence use across ten medical LLMs.
clinical_relevance: Medical LLM evaluation should test evidence application in clinical scenarios, not just guideline knowledge.
method: Built Med Evidence Bench with 1,536 physician-constructed Chinese-language items.
Tested guideline knowledge, standardized clinical scenarios and real-world laboratory scenarios.
Linked each medical-claim scoring criterion to a versioned source-text span.
evidence_signal: Across ten LLMs, Evidence Trace Scores fell from 0.975–0.997 for guideline knowledge to 0.182–0.447 for real-world scenarios; automated grading achieved macro-F1 0.930 against physician-majority judgments.
watch_item: Findings from Chinese-language materials do not establish clinical effectiveness, and automated grading agreement was lower for evidence application.
paper_title: An evidence-traceable benchmark of clinical reasoning in large language models
